chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Husayn al-Qala'ansi, who said:
I wrote to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the Predecessor, asking him about Al-Fuqqa', so he said: 'Do not approach it, for it is from the wine.'

key_terms.أَبِي الحَسَنِ المَاضِي: Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), the seventh Imam, often referred to as 'Al-Madi' (the Predecessor/Deceased) in later narrations.
key_terms.الخَمۡر: Wine (intoxicant), the primary reference for impurity and prohibition in Islamic law.
key_terms.الفُقَّاع: A type of fermented drink or vinegar, often derived from wine, discussed in fiqh regarding its purity and consumption.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on consuming or using Al-Fuqqa' in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the status of 'Al-Fuqa'' (a fermented drink or vinegar made from wine) by stating it is 'from the wine,' indicating its permissibility is tied to its origin or residual intoxicating properties. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that products derived from wine remain subject to the prohibition of wine unless the intoxicant is fully removed, a key distinction in *taharah* (purity) and *aklah* (consumption) laws.
